A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same study, with matching methods, figures and experiments. The supplied v2 ends after its references despite unresolved appendix citations; v3 supplies Appendix A. The reported content supports comparison without assuming any unseen earlier supplementary material.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, OOD detection, feature-alignment and ablation results for the proposed model in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: v3 retains original results for the proposed model and additionally reports ImageNet-Sketch generalization results in Table 3.

M1.justification: The T-distributed adapter, two-stage architecture, expert routing and KNN detection procedure remain. Section 2.3 newly explains decoder cross-attention, momentum soft targets and label smoothing, but the PDFs do not establish these disclosures as changes to the existing procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds ImageNet-Sketch evaluation with ImageNet as the source dataset, extending coverage to a photographic-to-sketch domain shift. The existing long-tailed classification, feature-alignment and OOD datasets remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds direct CLIP zero-shot, linear-probing and fine-tuning comparisons. The new ImageNet-Sketch comparison also includes CoOp, VPT and DAPT. These substantially broaden the comparison methods beyond the retained long-tailed recognition and OOD baselines.

E3.justification: Table 1 now reports both unmarked and explicitly designated 384×384 variants, alongside additional CLIP evaluation modes. Table 3 introduces an ImageNet-to-Sketch evaluation protocol. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish that those experiments were changed or rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds the ImageNet-Sketch distribution-shift test and a qualitative caption word-frequency analysis in Section 2.4. The existing adapter-stage and concentration-parameter ablation designs remain, with numerical revisions assessed under E6.

E5.justification: The feature-distance standard deviations in v2 Table 3 are retained unchanged in v3 Table 4. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests for the principal performance comparisons.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises ViT's reported ImageNet-LT overall accuracy from 52.4 to 31.6 and adds CLIP and resolution-specific result rows. The retained ablations change the proposed method's 69.6 to 69.4. New ImageNet-Sketch results report 50.2 for the proposed method versus 48.3 for DAPT. OOD and feature-alignment results remain unchanged; the resolution-specific additions do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 states the distribution and normalizer formulas but refers to an absent derivation. Appendix A.2 in v3 supplies tangent-normal decomposition, directional-distribution formulas, a Beta-variable characterization and a multistep normalization proof in Equations 9–23. This is substantial additional formal material.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: identifying multi-modal concept-drift problems, proposing the T-distributed adapter, improving pre-training and downstream adaptation, and introducing OpenMMlo. The additional comparisons support these existing claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets the CLIP comparisons as showing that high-quality pre-training cannot prevent downstream tail bias, and attributes ImageNet-Sketch performance to adapter robustness. It removes the low-learning-rate explanation for the limited movement of trainable concentration. The principal feature-crowding explanation remains.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 and Table 7 newly document architecture dimensions, optimizer settings, training budgets, batch sizes and A100 hardware. Appendix A.4 explains category-name masking and reports masked/unmasked data availability; Section 2.3 expands training details and the repository link changes. Reproducibility remains limited by conflicting step counts and learning rates between A.3 and Table 7.

R1.justification: The new four-part related-work section covers multi-modal models, long-tailed open-world learning, concept drift and hyperspherical distributions. It adds substantive discussion of direct antecedents, including Yang et al. (2023), and expands positioning relative to CLIP-based fine-tuning and existing drift methods. This exceeds the accompanying citation-style changes.

P1.justification: The main section order and most introductory and concluding prose remain. v3 edits grammar, expands architecture and dataset explanations, repairs appendix references, and moves the concept-drift/data-drift remark into Appendix A.1.3. These refine the retained narrative rather than extensively reorganizing it.

P2.justification: Table 1 substantially expands to display CLIP modes and resolution variants. v3 adds the generalization table, training-hyperparameter table and three-panel OpenMMlo example figure. Existing figures and other result tables are largely retained and reflowed within the conference layout.

improvement.justification: Resolution-labelled comparisons, direct CLIP baselines and the ImageNet-Sketch test make the empirical evidence more informative, while the appendices fill important documentation gaps in v2. However, A.3 conflicts with Table 7 on training budgets and learning rates, and the added derivation drops a factor of two in Equation 15. The revision improves transparency and empirical coverage, but these technical inconsistencies limit the overall quality gain.
